facts.claim: Nairobi began in 1899 as a British camp and supply depot for railway construction workers on Maasai land.

source.title: 5 Unique facts about Nairobi
source.author: Edwin Kis'sanya
source.quote: In 1899, the British "build a camp and supply depot for construction workers"

facts.claim: Nairobi began as a railway camp for the Uganda Railway.

source.title: Nairobi, Kenya (Research Starter)
source.author: Lynn-nore Chittom
source.quote: began as a railway camp for the Imperial British East Africa Company's Uganda Railway

facts.claim: The name comes from a Maasai phrase meaning cool waters (spelled Enkare Nairobi in one source, Ewaso Nyirobi in another).

source.title: 5 Unique facts about Nairobi
source.author: Edwin Kis'sanya
source.quote: The Maasai had called the land Enkare Nairobi because of its cool waters.

facts.claim: Nairobi's Maasai-phrase name is rendered as 'the place of cool water' (EBSCO spells it Ewaso Nyirobi; it also notes an earlier name, Mile 327).

source.title: Nairobi, Kenya (Research Starter)
source.author: Lynn-nore Chittom
source.quote: the place of cool water

facts.claim: Nairobi became capital of the British East Africa Protectorate in 1905.

source.title: Nairobi, Kenya (Research Starter)
source.author: Lynn-nore Chittom
source.quote: In 1905, Nairobi became the capital of the British East Africa Protectorate.

facts.claim: Kenya's independence in 1963 made Nairobi the capital of the independent country.

source.title: 5 Unique facts about Nairobi
source.author: Edwin Kis'sanya
source.quote: After independence, Kenya made it its capital in 1963.

source.quote: officially opened in 22nd September, 1930 and named Coryndon Museum in honour of Sir Robert Coryndon

timeline.claim: During the Mau Mau uprising, Operation Anvil sweeps Nairobi and detains about 16,500 people, mostly Kikuyu.

source.author: T. K. Welliver
source.quote: swept Nairobi sector by sector, rounding up some 16,500 people, mostly Kikuyu.

timeline.claim: Kenya becomes independent; Nairobi is its capital. The colonial-era museum is renamed National Museums of Kenya.

source.title: Museum Story
source.quote: On the attainment of independence in 1963, it was re-named NMK.

timeline.claim: The bombing of the US Embassy in Nairobi severely affects the economy.

source.title: Nairobi, Kenya (Research Starter)
source.author: Lynn-nore Chittom
source.quote: In 1998, the economy was severely impacted by the terrorist bombing of the US Embassy in Nairobi.

places.name: Nairobi National Museum
places.what: A museum run by National Museums of Kenya on Museum Hill, begun in 1910 by naturalists. Its permanent galleries cover human origins, mammals, Kenyan history and more.

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: Initiated in 1910 by a group of naturalists

source.title: Nairobi National Museum
source.quote: The Museum was initiated in 1910 by a group of enthusiastic naturalists.

facts.label: Opened
facts.value: Opened 22 September 1930 as the Coryndon Museum

source.title: Nairobi National Museum
source.quote: officially opened in 22nd September, 1930 and named Coryndon Museum in honour of Sir Robert Coryndon

facts.label: Reopened
facts.value: Reopened June 2008 under its current name

source.title: Nairobi National Museum
source.quote: The Museum later re-opened in June 2008 as the Nairobi National Museum

facts.label: Galleries
facts.value: Permanent galleries include The Cradle of Human Kind and The History of Kenya

places.name: Nairobi National Park
places.what: A wildlife park just outside central Nairobi, managed within the city's edge. EBSCO calls it the only wild game reserve within the city limits of a major metropolitan city.

source.title: EXPLAINER: Wild heart in the city: Why Nairobi National Park is one of a kind
source.author: Sharon Mwende
source.quote: Just a short drive from the central business district.

places.name: Gikomba Market
places.what: A large open-air secondhand clothing market in Nairobi. Al Jazeera calls it the largest secondhand market in East Africa.

facts.label: Scale
facts.value: Described as the largest secondhand market in East Africa

source.title: Kenyan designers make fashion statement against textile waste
source.author: Alyona Synenko
source.quote: the largest secondhand market in East Africa

source.title: Kenyan designers make fashion statement against textile waste
source.author: Alyona Synenko
source.quote: The Gikomba market alone provides employment to about 65,000 people.

facts.label: Trade
facts.value: Shoppers can find branded clothing at low prices (Reuters 2014)

source.title: Global business of secondhand clothes thrives in Kenya
source.author: Reuters
source.quote: shoppers in Nairobi's Gikomba market can turn up Tommy Hilfiger jeans

places.name: Karura Forest
places.what: A large urban forest in northern Nairobi. It sheltered Mau Mau fighters and later became a symbol of resistance to land grabbing.

source.title: Karura Forest and the Politics of Community-Based Conservation in Kenya
source.author: Adwera Loice and Ian Chebii
source.quote: Karura Forest is a 1,041 hectare urban sanctuary located in Kenya's capital, Nairobi.

facts.label: History
facts.value: Used by Mau Mau fighters during the liberation struggle

source.title: Karura Forest and the Politics of Community-Based Conservation in Kenya
source.author: Adwera Loice and Ian Chebii
source.quote: sanctuaries for Mau Mau freedom fighters

facts.label: Land allocation
facts.value: In 1998 almost a third was secretly allocated to developers

source.title: Forest History
source.quote: In 1998 almost a third of the forest was allocated secretly to developers.
